items.headline: Man who walked dementia widow home returned to rape her, admits guilt
items.summary: Mohamad Zakir Jaafar, 55, pleaded guilty on 7 July to two rape charges and one of outrage of modesty against a 71-year-old widow with severe dementia. Prosecutors are seeking about 15 to 16 years' jail and 12 months in lieu of caning after the victim's son found CCTV footage of an assault at her flat.

items.headline: Opposition figure Lim Tean ordered to begin jail term on 20 July
items.summary: Lawyer and People's Alliance for Reform co-founder Lim Tean, 61, has been ordered to surrender on 20 July to serve three months and one week in jail for practising law without a valid certificate. The Court of Appeal on 6 July refused his bid to challenge the enhanced sentence.

items.headline: Go-Ahead takes over Tampines bus routes from SBS Transit after 40 years
items.summary: Go-Ahead Singapore began running the 27-route Tampines bus package on 5 July under a five-year, S$646 million contract, ending SBS Transit's four decades of service in the town. Go-Ahead won the tender with the highest overall score.

items.headline: 280 motorcyclists screened at Admiralty Road West; 15 caught unlicensed
items.summary: A multi-agency operation at Admiralty Road West screened about 280 motorcyclists on 29 June and caught 15 riders, aged 24 to 59, without a valid licence or insurance. One foreign-registered motorcycle was impounded for lacking a vehicle entry permit.

items.headline: Singapore Garden Festival returns to Gardens by the Bay for 10th edition
items.summary: The 10th Singapore Garden Festival runs from 4 to 12 July at Gardens by the Bay, with a Bayfront Green MarketPlace of 90 vendors selling plants, gardening accessories, and botanical collectables.

items.headline: India coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The Brief could not reach any of its allowed India outlets (The Hindu, The Indian Express, Hindustan Times, The Times of India, NDTV, The Economic Times) after repeated attempts; all returned egress-policy or crawler blocks. No India items are carried today rather than cite unverified sources.

items.headline: UK coverage is unavailable in today's edition
items.summary: The Brief could not reach BBC or Sky News, its allowed UK outlets, after repeated attempts; both returned egress-policy blocks. To avoid citing unverified sources, no UK-domestic items are carried today.

items.headline: Nigel Farage resigns as MP amid funding scandal, forcing a by-election
items.summary: Reform UK leader Nigel Farage resigned his Commons seat on 7 July while facing a parliamentary standards inquiry into an undeclared 5 million pound donation from Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne, and a second probe over benefits from convicted fraudster George Cottrell. Labour, the Conservatives, and the Liberal Democrats say they will not contest the by-election he has triggered.

items.headline: Sara Duterte's impeachment trial opens in the Philippine Senate
items.summary: The Senate impeachment trial of Vice-President Sara Duterte opened on 6 July in Manila on charges including the misuse of 612.5 million pesos in confidential funds and alleged threats against President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. Conviction would require 16 of the 24 senators.

items.headline: Russian missiles hit Kyiv for the third time in a week
items.summary: Russian missile strikes on Kyiv on 7 July killed at least three people and wounded 14, including a 17-year-old, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. It was the third barrage to hit the Ukrainian capital in a single week.

items.headline: Trump declares the Iran ceasefire 'over' after a fresh exchange of strikes
items.summary: Speaking at the NATO summit on 8 July, US President Donald Trump declared the three-week-old US-Iran ceasefire 'over' after Iran's Revolutionary Guard struck US sites in Bahrain and Kuwait and US forces launched new strikes near the Strait of Hormuz. Trump threatened a naval blockade but said talks could still continue.

items.headline: UN inquiry demands release of Gaza doctor held by Israel for 18 months
items.summary: The UN's independent commission of inquiry on 8 July called for the immediate release of Dr Hussam Abu Safia, the 52-year-old director of Gaza's Kamal Adwan Hospital, held by Israel without charge for more than 18 months. It cited credible reports of 'continued and severe abuse.'

items.headline: SambaNova raises $1 billion at an $11 billion valuation for AI chips
items.summary: AI chipmaker SambaNova has raised $1 billion in a first close of its Series F, led by General Atlantic at an $11 billion post-money valuation, months after its last major round. A second close is expected in the coming weeks, and JPMorgan Chase signed on as an inference-infrastructure partner.

items.headline: ECB orders eurozone banks to plan for frontier-AI cyber threats
items.summary: The European Central Bank's top supervisor, Claudia Buch, has told eurozone banks to submit action plans by the end of October to counter cybersecurity threats posed by frontier AI models, opening a new regulatory front on AI risk.

items.headline: Bank of America U-turns on an OpenAI loan to chase its IPO
items.summary: Bank of America, which had earlier judged OpenAI too risky, reversed course on a loan to the ChatGPT maker in a bid to secure a role in the company's planned public listing.

items.headline: Tencent seeks to sell up to $1.6 billion Kuaishou stake in AI pivot
items.summary: Tencent is looking to sell up to $1.6 billion of its stake in short-video company Kuaishou, redirecting capital as it accelerates its artificial-intelligence investment push.

items.headline: Tech layoffs that name-check AI top 120,000 roles in 2026
items.summary: TechCrunch's running tally puts 2026 tech layoffs that cited AI as a factor at about 120,000 roles, including Atlassian's cut of roughly 1,600 jobs, or 10% of its staff, to rebalance toward AI and enterprise sales.

items.headline: Wall Street ends mixed as Iran tensions drag the Dow lower
items.summary: Wall Street ended mixed on 8 July: the Dow fell 576.76 points, or 1.09%, to 52,348.39 and the S&P 500 slipped 0.28% to 7,482.71, while the Nasdaq edged up 0.2% to 25,870.65, after President Trump called the Iran ceasefire 'over.'

items.headline: Fed's June minutes reveal a split over the path for interest rates
items.summary: Minutes of the Federal Reserve's June meeting, released on 8 July, showed officials divided on rates: nine of 19 projected at least one hike in 2026, eight projected none, and one a cut, with rates held at 3.50% to 3.75%.

items.headline: Levi Strauss beats estimates and raises its full-year guidance
items.summary: Levi Strauss beat expectations with second-quarter sales up about 8% to $1.56 billion and lifted its full-year sales-growth outlook to 7% to 7.5% and adjusted earnings to $1.46 to $1.52 a share, despite tariff pressure on margins.

items.headline: ITV agrees to sell its media arm to Comcast's Sky for up to 1.6 billion pounds
items.summary: ITV agreed to sell its broadcasting and streaming business, including its free-to-air channels and ITVX, to Comcast's Sky for as much as 1.6 billion pounds ($2.1 billion), with around 950 million pounds to be returned to shareholders.

items.headline: Thales wins Exail Technologies with a 3.9 billion euro deal, beating Safran
items.summary: France's Thales agreed to buy Exail Technologies, a maker of drones and navigation systems, for 3.9 billion euros ($4.5 billion), outbidding rival Safran for the defence specialist.

items.headline: 🎾 Zverev beats Fritz to reach his first Wimbledon semi-final
items.summary: Alexander Zverev ended a seven-match losing run against Taylor Fritz, winning 6-4, 6-4, 6-2 to reach his first Wimbledon semi-final, where he meets British wild card Arthur Fery on 10 July.

items.headline: 🎾 British wild card Arthur Fery stuns Cobolli to reach the semis
items.summary: British wild card Arthur Fery, ranked outside the world's top 100, beat ninth seed Flavio Cobolli 6-4, 7-6(4), 6-0 to reach the Wimbledon semi-finals at his home Grand Slam.

items.headline: 🏏 Cornered India face England in the fourth T20I at Bristol
items.summary: India, 2-0 down, face England in the fourth T20I at Bristol on 9 July. England can clinch the series with a win, while India seek their first victory of the white-ball tour after a record 125-run defeat at Trent Bridge.

items.headline: 🏎️ Russell says Antonelli 'deserves to be ahead' before Spa
items.summary: Ahead of the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa on 17-19 July, Mercedes' George Russell said team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli 'deserves to be ahead' in the title fight, adding that 'I need to be better.'

items.headline: 🏎️ Mercedes drivers address contracts amid Verstappen rumours
items.summary: Mercedes drivers George Russell and Kimi Antonelli addressed their contract situations amid continued speculation over Max Verstappen's future, as Formula 1 heads to the Belgian Grand Prix at Spa.

items.headline: Blood protein GDF15 may flag dementia risk decades before symptoms
items.summary: A large multi-cohort analysis found that people under 55 with elevated levels of the blood protein GDF15 had a significantly raised risk of later developing dementia, especially vascular dementia, pointing to a possible early screening biomarker.

items.headline: Long-held dogma that female mammals can't make new eggs may be wrong
items.summary: Scientific American reports mounting evidence that adult ovaries in mice, cows, pigs, primates, and humans harbour cells that can generate new egg cells. Northeastern biologist Jonathan Tilly says the finding challenges the assumption that females are born with a fixed egg supply.

items.headline: Machine learning uncovers new antibiotics for drug-resistant gonorrhoea
items.summary: Researchers used a machine-learning screen to identify antibiotics with fresh mechanisms against Neisseria gonorrhoeae, including two candidates structurally unlike existing drugs, as the pathogen grows resistant to nearly all current treatments.

items.headline: Apes and humans have shared rhythmic laughter for 15 million years
items.summary: An analysis of 140 laughter sequences from orangutans, gorillas, bonobos, chimpanzees, and humans found all produce evenly spaced, isochronous laughter, implying their last common ancestor laughed rhythmically about 15 million years ago.

fun_fact.headline: Vantablack absorbs up to 99.965% of visible light
fun_fact.body: Vantablack, created by the British firm Surrey NanoSystems in 2014, absorbs up to 99.965% of visible light — so little escapes that a crumpled, three-dimensional surface coated in it looks like a flat black void. The colour comes not from a pigment but from a dense forest of carbon nanotubes that trap incoming light and bounce it around until it is lost as heat.

puzzle.title: The Marching Column
puzzle.body:
A column of soldiers 20 metres long marches forward at a steady pace. A dog starts at the very back, runs at a constant speed straight to the front of the column, then immediately turns and runs back to the rear. It arrives back at the rear at the exact moment the column has advanced 20 metres from where it began.

How far, in total, did the dog run?
puzzle.approach: Work with relative speeds — the gap the dog closes and reopens depends on how fast the column moves.
puzzle.answer:
About 48.28 metres — exactly 20(1 + √2) metres.

Let the column's speed be c and the dog's speed be d, with column length L = 20 m. Running to the front, the dog closes the 20 m gap at relative speed (d − c), taking L/(d − c). Running back, it meets the rear at relative speed (d + c), taking L/(d + c). The total time equals the time for the column to advance its own length, L/c.

So L/(d−c) + L/(d+c) = L/c  →  2d/(d²−c²) = 1/c  →  d² − 2cd − c² = 0  →  d = c(1 + √2).

The dog runs for time L/c, so its distance = d·(L/c) = (1 + √2)·20 ≈ 48.28 m.

word_puzzle.title: Around the Block
word_puzzle.body:
Letters sit on the four sides of a square. Spell words of three or more letters using all 12 letters. Consecutive letters may never come from the same side, and each new word must begin with the previous word's last letter. It can be solved in just TWO words.

   Top:     P · U · T
   Right:   E · O · N
   Bottom:  L · Y · R
   Left:    A · G · D
word_puzzle.approach: Use every letter at least once; two consecutive letters can never come from the same side, and each new word must begin with the previous word's last letter.
word_puzzle.answer:
PLAYGROUND → DUET.

PLAYGROUND uses P, L, A, Y, G, R, O, U, N, D. DUET begins with D (PLAYGROUND's last letter) and adds U, E, and T — covering all 12 letters. No two consecutive letters ever share a side.
